news.title: From Wembley wizard to World Cup woe, Billy Gilmour looks back on 50 Scotland caps
news.lede: Billy Gilmour has come a long way since his early days as a young, hot Scotland prospect, and his headline grabbing performance on his first start for his country against England at Wembley in the Euros. “I remember that,” Gilmour said. Before adding, rather candidly; “I was s******g myself.” It is a little hard to believe that the fresh-faced youth who conquered those nerves to run the show at the home of the Auld Enemy and announce himself on the international scene is about to pick up his 50th Scotland cap, with his certain selection against Slovenia tonight ensuring he will earn his place on the national team roll of honour.

news.title: Everything you need to know about the CAF Strategy Conference: Dates, venue and key issues
news.lede: The Confédération Africaine de Football (CAF) will bring together leading decision-makers, coaches and football experts in Cape Verde in October for a landmark Strategy Conference aimed at shaping the next phase of African football development. The three-day gathering will take place from 7 to 9 October 2026 in Santa Maria, Sal Island, and will be convened under the leadership of CAF President Dr Patrice Motsepe. The Conference comes after Africa’s record participation at the FIFA World Cup 2026, where 10 national teams represented the continent and nine progressed to the knockout stages. Their performances will form an important part of discussions as CAF examines what worked, what can be improved and how African teams can become even more competitive by the FIFA World Cup 2030.

news.title: World Cup winner reveals 15-year health battle with illness that leaves sufferers in bed for 'months'
news.lede: Gattuso admitted that he retired after being diagnosed with an autoimmune disease that he has been battling since. The iconic midfielder hung up his boots in 2013 after an impressive playing career spanning almost two decades. And he has now opened up about his long-term struggles with his illness that takes a toll on him on a daily basis. Speaking at the Festival dello Sport, Gattuso revealed: "I stopped playing because of the autoimmune disease I got.

news.title: Modric hopes fans back Croatia against Spain after England shame
news.lede: Croatia captain Luka Modric said he hoped the country's fans would support the team despite a hefty defeat by England when they face world champions Spain on Tuesday in the Nations League. Modric and his team-mates were crushed 7-0 at home by Thomas Tuchel's England on Saturday and the AC Milan midfielder said afterwards he was "ashamed" of the team's performance. Croatia host Spain in Split in Group A3 seeking to make amends, while La Roja are hoping to seal qualification to the quarter-finals. "Losing isn't the problem, but the way we lost is," 41-year-old former Real Madrid star Modric told reporters Monday.

news.title: CAF Strategy Conference: Carlos Queiroz – five World Cups and a Ghana campaign with lessons for Africa
news.lede: Carlos Queiroz will arrive at the CAF Strategy Conference in Cabo Verde only days after his spell as Ghana coach came to an end, but carrying with him another chapter in one of international football’s most travelled coaching careers. The 73-year-old mutually ended his agreement with the Ghana Football Association on 1 October, just weeks after being handed a new mandate following the FIFA World Cup 2026. Despite leaving the Black Stars, Queiroz will still attend the Conference in Sal to share the experience of guiding Ghana through one of the most demanding groups at the World Cup and into the knockout stage for the first time since 2010.

news.title: Tebas Calls Real Madrid ‘Most Rebellious Team’ in Spanish Football
news.lede: Rabat - LaLiga president Javier Tebas has described Real Madrid as the “most rebellious” club in Spanish professional football, criticizing how the club’s leadership views the sport's future structure. Tebas made the comments on Monday during the first National Conference on Journalism and Sport in Vigo, organized by the Galician Association of Sports Journalists (AGAXORDE). “The most rebellious team in Spain is Real Madrid because Madrid’s directors have a way of understanding football that I do not have,” Tebas said. “In Europe, there is Al-Khelaifi.”
